chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman from Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah al-Khazzaz from Harun ibn Harijah from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He said to me, 'O Harun ibn Harijah, what is the distance between you and the Mosque of Kufa? It is one mile.' I said, 'No.' He said, 'Do you pray all the prayers there?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'If I were present there, I would hope that no prayer would be missed by me in it. And do you know the virtue of that place? No righteous servant or prophet has not prayed in your mosque, even the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). When Allah took him on the Night Journey, He said to him, 'Gabriel (peace be upon him), do you know where you are at this moment? You are opposite the Mosque of Kufa.' He said, 'Ask permission for me from my Lord, Exalted and Majestic, so that I may go to it and pray two rak'ahs in it.' So Allah, Exalted and Majestic, asked permission for him and granted it. And its right side is a garden from the gardens of Paradise, and its middle is a garden from the gardens of Paradise, and its rear is a garden from the gardens of Paradise. And the obligatory prayer in it equals a thousand prayers, and the voluntary prayer in it equals five hundred prayers, and sitting in it without recitation or remembrance is worship. And if people knew what is in it, they would come to it, even if crawling.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance and reward of praying in the Mosque of Kufa according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the spiritual hierarchy of the Mosque of Kufa, linking its sanctity to the Prophet’s Night Journey (Isra) where Jibril identified the site. The text emphasizes the quantitative merit of worship there, stating that obligatory prayers equal a thousand and voluntary prayers equal five hundred, while mere presence is deemed an act of devotion, reflecting the Shia scholarly view of Kufa as a central axis of religious authority.
